```plato
    //==
    // # The shared point-list formulas
    //
    // The formulas every point-list shape in the line, planar-shape, polygon and
    // spatial-primitive files is built from. They take a plain `Array<Point2D>` /
    // `Array<Point3D>` rather than an interface so that a shape whose points are NOT its
    // `PointSet` members (a regular polygon's computed vertices, a polygon's holes) can
    // call them too. Aggregate reductions (centroid-of-points, bounds-of-points, total
    // polyline length) are folded through the P2 IIndexable Reduce/Map family: the
    // kernels below materialize their elements once and reduce. IDifference.Between(a, b)
    // yields (b - a) — pinned in the algebra interfaces — so the sign of BoundsSize and
    // every Between-based delta below rests on a documented convention, not observed
    // behavior.

    //==
    // # Point-list kernels
    //
    // The formulas every point-list shape in `lines.types.plato`, `planar.types.plato`,
    // `polygons.types.plato` and the `spatial-*.types.plato` files is built from. They take a
    // plain `Array<Point2D>` / `Array<Point3D>` rather than an interface so that a
    // shape whose points are NOT its `PointSet` members (a regular polygon's
    // computed vertices, a polygon's holes) can call them too.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here and inherited by every caller:
    //   * Winding: counter-clockwise is positive (README / CONVENTIONS.md - Winding).
    //     `ShoelaceArea` is SIGNED; the `Area` obligations take its absolute value.
    //   * Vertex order: a closed ring lists each vertex once; the closing edge from
    //     the last vertex back to the first is implicit (hence `AtModulo`).
    //   * Containment is the even-odd (crossing) rule and is exact only for a
    //     SIMPLE ring. On the boundary itself the answer is whatever the floating
    //     point comparison happens to give — see `PolygonContainsPoint`.

    // Twice the signed area of triangle (a, b, c): the z component of
    // (b - a) x (c - a). Positive when a -> b -> c turns counter-clockwise, zero
    // when the three points are collinear. The primitive orientation predicate.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curve_orientation
    TwiceSignedArea(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D): Number
        => (b.X - a.X) * (c.Y - a.Y) - (b.Y - a.Y) * (c.X - a.X);
```
